title: Free choice not extinguished but weakened (Trent, Session 6, canon 5)
source_text: VI. Itaque pertendunt Liberum arbitrium, respectu boni ipsius salutaris, per peccatum extinctum & amissum non esse, sed solum debilitatum, fauciatum & attenuatum. Qua in re sequuntur doctrinam Synodi Tridentinae, cujus hic quoque Canon est quintus Sessionis sextae. Si quis liberum hominis arbitrium post Adae peccatum amissum & extinctum esse dixerit, aut rem esse de solo titulo, imo titulum sine re, figmentum denique a Satana invectum in Ecclesiam: anathema sit.
pass_a_gloss: VI. Therefore they contend that free Choice, in respect of saving good itself, has not been extinguished and lost through sin, but only weakened, wounded and attenuated. In which matter they follow the doctrine of the Tridentine Synod, whose Canon here also is the fifth of the sixth Session. If anyone shall say that the free choice of man after Adam's sin has been lost and extinguished, or that it is a thing of title only, nay a title without a thing, a fiction finally brought into the Church by Satan: let him be anathema.
pass_b_english: So they maintain that free choice, even with respect to saving good, was not extinguished and lost through sin, but only weakened, wounded and diminished. Here they follow the teaching of the Synod of Trent, whose canon on this point is the fifth of the sixth session:

'If anyone says that man's free choice was lost and extinguished after Adam's sin, or that it is a thing in name only, indeed a name without a reality, in short a fiction brought into the Church by Satan: let him be anathema.'
